title: Adaptive Exploration for Latent-State Bandits

problem.claim: The setting involves bandits with rewards governed by an unobserved Markov state that evolves independently of learner actions, while the optimal arm may change.

gap.claim: The learner must adapt to changing optimal arms using only past actions and rewards, without directly observing the latent state.

contributions.claim: Algorithms augment LinUCB with a lagged action-reward summary and, when available, a multi-arm probe fingerprint of the hidden state.
Adaptive variants refresh probe fingerprints using residual, margin, and staleness tests.
Synthetic stress tests report lower dynamic regret than standard, adversarial, and non-stationary bandit baselines under sufficiently discriminative and frequently updated summaries.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Synthetic stress tests vary state count, transition rate, noise, and horizon and report reduced dynamic regret relative to several bandit baselines.
Ablations and misspecification tests report weak fingerprint separation, high noise, and state changes during sequential probes as main failure modes.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper studies latent-state Markov bandits with action-independent state evolution.
The optimal arm can change although the learner observes only actions and rewards.
The proposed algorithms provide LinUCB with lagged action-reward and optional probe-fingerprint summaries, refreshed adaptively.
Stress tests report lower dynamic regret under adequate state separation and update frequency, while ablations identify failure modes.

source_observation.claim: Latent-state summaries are supplied to LinUCB, with fingerprints refreshed according to residual, margin, and staleness tests.

interpretation.claim: Adaptive summary refresh may help decision policies track changing hidden regimes.

application.claim: In partially observed sequential decisions, combine lightweight historical summaries with selectively refreshed probes.

exception.claim: The approach may fail when fingerprints do not separate states, noise is high, or states change during probes.

unknowns: No regret bounds or formal guarantees are stated.
The abstract does not specify real-world evaluation or detailed algorithmic implementation.
The magnitude and statistical significance of reported improvements are unspecified.
